## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) with \(t>r+s-n\), \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is the unique bigrassmannian \(v_1\cdots v_n\in S_n\) with \(\Des(v)=\{(r\leftrightarrow r+1)\}\), \(\Des(v^{-1})=\{(s\leftrightarrow s+1)\}\), \(v_t=s+1\), and
  \[
  v_{r,s,t,n}=(1,\ldots,t-1,\ s+1,\ldots,s+r-t+1,\ t,\ldots,s,\ s+r-t+2,\ldots,n).
  \]
  [source-2, lines 973-992]
- [source-backed] The source sets \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and states that \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is \(r\)-grassmannian and corresponds to the \(j\times i\) rectangle \(i^j\). [source-2, lines 1354-1362]
- [source-backed] In the integral symmetric-function setting, \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\); \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the ideal spanned by \(s_\lambda\) for \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\). The source states that \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of this quotient by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2, lines 1310-1325; source-2, lines 1365-1375]
- [source-backed] Theorem 5.4 sets
  \[
  a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\qquad b=\min(i,j),
  \]
  and gives the two generating sets
  \[
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},
  \qquad
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}
  \]
  for \(J_v\) as an ideal of \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [source-2, lines 1380-1402]
- [source-backed] Both displayed Theorem 5.4 families have \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements; their degree generating function is \(q^{ij}\qbin{a+b}{a}\). [source-2, lines 1407-1421]
- [source-backed] The formal conjecture is: “The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem [5.4] are both minimal.” The authors report computer verification only for all bigrassmannian permutations with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1489-1502]
- [source-backed] With \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Lambda_n\) the graded ring of symmetric functions over \(\mathbb Z\) and \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), the source conjectures that \(M/\Lambda_+M\) requires \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators and suspects
  \[
  M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}.
  \]
  It states that a proof had eluded the authors. [source-2, lines 1517-1552]
- [source-backed] The related type-\(A_{n-1}\) open question asks for a minimal generating set of \(I_w\), at least for varieties defined by inclusions (there stated to avoid \(4231,35142,42513,351624\)) or smooth varieties (there stated to avoid \(3412,4231\)). [source-2, lines 1913-1929]
- [source-backed] \(\Lambda_+\) occurs in the proposition and its application, but the supplied source passage does not explicitly define \(\Lambda_+\); only the grading \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Lambda_n\) is stated. [source-2, lines 1520-1540]

## Strategy
Use the integral \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) formulation and the two explicit families above. Any quotient-based minimality argument must first obtain an exact definition of \(\Lambda_+\) and then apply the stated graded-module proposition.

## Gaps
- No independent definition of \(J_v\), nor an explicit specification of the parabolic \(J\) in terms of \(r\), occurs in the supplied excerpts.
- “Minimal” in the formal conjecture is not explicitly defined there; the later proposition defines minimality “with respect to inclusion,” but this should not be silently imposed on the conjecture. [source-2, lines 1495-1499; source-2, lines 1529-1533]
- At lines 1294–1307, the text begins with grassmannian \(w\) but says “we say \(u\) is \(r\)-grassmannian”; this is an apparent \(u/w\) variable mismatch. No correction is supplied. [source-2, lines 1294-1307]
- The supplied material does not formally define the partition-concatenation notation \(((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\) or \((i^j,b^a)\), beyond its geometric description. [source-2, lines 1407-1413]

## Next
Obtain exact source grounding for the definition of \(J_v\), the relevant \(J\), and \(\Lambda_+\) before attempting a minimality proof via \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\).
